title: Toby and Pipkin's Rolling Boxes
markdown:
In a quiet town where sunbeams lay softly lived Toby the bridge maker and Pipkin the hamster. They helped Auntie Flo at her Scooter Store. One warm morning Flo wanted to move some lovely new scooter boxes.

“These boxes are so very heavy to lift.”

Toby and Pipkin tried nudging. The boxes moved only a tiny bit, a sulky scrape. They tried pulling; paws slipped; the boxes stayed put, as if they had decided to be furniture.

Toby watched a little ladybug tumble down a small mossy slope. “Look, Pipkin. It rolled down all by itself.”

Pipkin remembered his toy cart, which rolled more easily than when he dragged it, wheels ticking like a tiny clock. Toby’s eyes lit. “If we can make the boxes roll down…”

Together they found a long, smooth board in the back of the shop, the sort Flo used for ramps on rainy days. Toby placed one end on the floor and the other on a low step, a gentle slope, not a cliff. “Let’s try one box.”

They nudged a scooter box onto the board. A gentle push. The box rolled smoothly, quietly, oh-so-gently down the ramp and stopped where Flo could reach the tape. “Oh!” squeaked Pipkin.

Flo smiled. “Wonderful. It rolls so easily. You two are clever.”

Each box followed with the same gentle ease. Toby walked beside the last one so it would not hurry. Pipkin sat on the step like a very small traffic warden.

They looked at each other, hearts full. A smooth sloping pathway helped heavy boxes roll. “A little bridge for them to roll along,” Toby said.

Pipkin nodded, bright eyes a little heavy, thinking of other things that might prefer rolling to dragging. Afternoon laid long sleepy shadows. The work was done. They did not snuggle into a sermon about dreams. Flo locked the shop. Toby wiped the board and leaned it where they would find it tomorrow. Pipkin checked the empty corner where the boxes had been, then checked it again, because hamsters like to be sure.
